executiveSummary: GM0173's official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, contained centre, 32,021 residents, fourteen neighbourhoods, two BAG woonplaatsen, one BRT woonkern and Twente safety-region assignment are coherent. Neighbourhood population is one below the municipality total (-0.003%) and can be reconciled without changing rounded observations. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes its numerical gate, but its Oldenzaal interpretation is not release-ready. Oldenzaal's official climate atlas says direct Dinkel-overflow effects are negligible because the city lies on a stuwwal; the major-river preset nevertheless publishes an exact 0.455443 m local inundation, 2,249 affected resident-equivalents and unchanged service consequences through T+72 without a selected local stream, runoff or hydraulic case. Eight unrelated active hazards reuse exactly one full fourteen-neighbourhood severity order. The canonical wildfire has zero local flame despite Het Hulsbeek's woodland, recreation and event exposure, while a controlled hypothetical source at the official Het Hulsbeek neighbourhood centre ranks its source neighbourhood only fourth. A June 2026 Vitens plan identifies a conditional regional shortage, staged pressure reduction and De Essen, De Graven Es and De Thij as potentially more affected, but the heat preset's exact water trajectory does not implement those triggers or spatial rules. Resident-only exposure omits events with published attendance orders above the resident population, including 100,000-150,000 carnival visitors and about 20,000 Hulsbeekdag visitors. Dutch road links, a station and scheduled stops omit the operational A1 and Oldenzaal-Bad Bentheim freight/passenger rail chain, German continuity, hazardous-goods response, internal viaducts and external acute care. Static registers, current pages, conditional plans, dated observations and missing topology retain their own time and scope; absent observations are Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0173 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement input
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK snapshot retrieved 2026-08-31; BRT source date 2025-07-01
supports: CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0173 as Oldenzaal in Overijssel and reports 32,021 residents, density 1,486/km2, 25.3% aged 65 or older and 5,235 one-person households. The generated centre [6.90526743455187, 52.30936320378356] is inside the generalized boundary.

Fourteen neighbourhood rows in fourteen districts sum to 32,020 residents, one below the municipality total (-0.003%); households sum to 14,475 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 8,105. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 32,021 without rewriting source observations.

The active BAG woonplaatsen are Deurningen and Oldenzaal; the independently assigned BRT settlement layer contains one Oldenzaal woonkern. BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and the regional bundle reports CBS CC BY 4.0.

All fourteen rows contain the core demographic, housing, land and water fields. Cars per household covers 11/14; district heat and public charging cover 0/14. Missing, suppressed, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — NWB-Light, rail and scheduled-transit context consumed by the simulator
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 2026-08-01; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 2026-08-31/2026-09-03; public NWB and ProRail geometry CC0 1.0
supports: Nine Dutch logical border links represent A1, N342, N343, N733, N734, N735 and N736 connections to Losser, Dinkelland and Enschede. The two A1 edges share NWB-road-1 and the two N342 edges share NWB-road-342; each pair is consecutive series geometry, not independent capacity.
Nominal capacities 260 and 150 are synthetic scenario units and route eligibility is limited to Mobility and assumed road Supply, not observed emergency throughput or physical utility topology.

One ProRail station point, Oldenzaal, lies inside GM0173. Sixty-five GTFS stop areas show scheduled transport context, not scenario-time trains, buses, passengers, vehicles, accessible capacity, closures or evacuation throughput.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Oldenzaal climate atlas and local stuwwal, rain, heat, drought and flood semantics
evidenceSources.edition: current municipal climate-atlas explanation accessed 2026-09-03; underlying maps are 2050 model context; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality distinguishes living on a keileem/sand stuwwal from a peat-bearing stream valley. It says beeks and ponds on the stuwwal depend entirely on rainfall, so drought affects water quality, nature and the productivity of the drinking-water area.

It reports increasing pluvial risk despite Blue Arteries and other measures, and possible apparent temperatures up to 46 degrees Celsius at multiple urban locations, industrial areas and Het Hulsbeek in a heatwave.

It explicitly describes the direct effect of Dinkel flooding on Oldenzaal as negligible because of the stuwwal location. This contradicts treating a generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel proximity function as a precise direct municipality inundation.
The atlas is a modelled 2050 vulnerability view and does not state event probability, live rainfall, groundwater, sewer state, current surface temperature or a T+72 forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Documented heavy-rain pathways and municipal drainage measures
evidenceSources.edition: current municipal guidance accessed 2026-09-03; Gemeentelijk Rioleringsplan 2021-2025 retained as historical design context; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality states that short intense rain can exceed sewer processing, leave water on streets, enter lower areas and homes, inundate viaducts and temporarily close road sections.

Named measures include larger sewers, separated Blue Arteries, underground and surface buffers, wadis, enlargement of Stakenbeek storage/discharge, reduced inflow through Plan De Hulst and routing rainwater toward less harmful locations.

The Glinde-Hooiland improvement plan separately shows a 70 mm/hour stress-test pattern with and without sewer operation and names Blue Arteries and storage. A design/stress-test map or completed measure is not observed event depth, remaining storage, pump state, road passability or guaranteed recovery.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — RWZI Oldenzaal design decision and public water-system context
evidenceSources.edition: board decision 2023-09-26; HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated for decision, HWH data CC BY-SA 4.0
supports: The water board agreed design assumptions to reduce RWZI Oldenzaal intake from 4,060 to at most 3,500 m3/hour and include expected future loads of about 2,000 household and 9,000 industrial pollution-equivalents in the design. The installation was to be adapted for effluent quality and ageing components.

The public HWH snapshot assigns 82 points to GM0173: RWZI Oldenzaal and 81 weirs, including structures named Stakenbeek, Hulsbeek, Elsmors, Coulissenweg N342 and A1 junction 32. The national aggregation is explicitly partial.

A board design decision and asset register do not establish the current connected catchment, flow direction, compatible live capacity, storage, control state, power backup, bypass, quality, damage, repair or T+72 operation. The RWZI and all observed weir capacities are null in the app context.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel and crisis-planning governance
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Risicoprofiel, policy plan, fire-service coverage profile and care-risk profile adopted 2026-04-23 and published 2026-06-02; official-publication reuse terms apply
supports: The Twente safety-region board formally adopted its Regionaal Risicoprofiel, 2026-2029 policy plan, fire-service coverage plan, multidisciplinary training plan and care-risk profile.

The published preceding detailed Twente annex identifies nature fire, extreme weather, electricity failure, drinking-water contamination, telecom/ICT disruption, fast-road accidents, hazardous substances on rail, care incidents and event panic as relevant scenarios.

Regional planning documents establish governance and relevant mechanisms, not a selected incident, municipal probability field, available appliance/crew roster, hospital capacity or automatic T+72 restoration curve.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Authoritative nature-fire scenario factors and time-to-evacuate semantics
evidenceSources.edition: regional risk-profile annex published 2022-12; superseded for governance by the 2026 adoption but retained as cited mechanism context; reuse licence not stated
supports: The Twente annex says nature-fire outcome depends on season/weather, fuels, recreation and vulnerable objects, access, extinguishing-water availability, safe deployment, escape routes and the self-reliance of residents and visitors.

It explicitly frames nature-fire evacuation time as hours rather than days and says large-scale water transport takes time to establish because water availability is relatively limited compared with fuel and area.

Those qualitative and regional scenario statements cannot be converted into a current ignition, local fuel-moisture surface, perimeter, visitor count, route capacity, response time or live fire probability.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Dynamic nature-fire phase and incident mapping semantics
evidenceSources.edition: dynamic national page observed 2026-09-03 with Twente at Phase 1; page states daily assessment; reuse licence not stated
supports: Twente displayed Phase 1 at access. The phase is assessed daily from weather, field observations, land-manager and fire-service information and can be changed around midnight.

Brandweer guidance says people should flee quickly toward a public road, hard surface or built-up area, move perpendicular to the fire, help others and give an exact location to 112. It cautions that mobile coverage may be poor in nature areas.

Brandweer Twente reported in March 2026 that high-expansion-risk fire reports can trigger drone deployment and automated infrared-derived fire polygons. A current phase or response capability is observed/operational context, not an ignition, future phase, guaranteed drone availability, suppression result or model perimeter.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Recreation and event exposure in the city and Het Hulsbeek
evidenceSources.edition: integral events policy published 2023 with 2022 event inventory; current tourism page checked 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipal event inventory reports about 20,000 Hulsbeekdag visitors. The current municipal tourism page identifies Het Hulsbeek as a recreation area and reports 100,000-150,000 annual carnival-procession visitors.
A municipal report on 2026-05-24 described Het Hulsbeek as busy on a warm day, confirming that weather and recreation can produce material transient occupancy.

Event estimates and a past busy-day description establish dynamic-population relevance, not current attendance, precise location, visitor vulnerability, transport mode, egress demand or future event scheduling.

evidenceSources.title: E10 — Oldenzaal-Bad Bentheim international rail and 2025 freight context
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 freight-traffic annual report published 2026; reuse licence not stated
supports: ProRail reports 7,850 freight trains at the Oldenzaal-Bentheim border crossing in 2025, up 22% from 2024, with the corridor share of Netherlands-Germany rail freight rising from 15% to 19% during third-track diversions.

Current ProRail project pages describe the Oldenzaal station, Amersfoort-Bad Bentheim international corridor, regional and Berlin passenger operation, planned capacity changes and cross-border cooperation.

Annual train totals and infrastructure plans do not identify incident-time consist contents, hazardous substances, train location, track availability, passenger load, German operating state, evacuation capacity or emergency access.

evidenceSources.title: E11 — Conditional 2026 Noordoost-Twente drinking-water pressure-reduction plan
evidenceSources.edition: operator page dated/updated 2026-06-17 and accessed 2026-09-03; conditional summer plan, reuse licence not stated
supports: Vitens says Noordoost-Twente has little extra drinking-water reserve, works as one connected regional system and cannot quickly add extraction or import. High warm-weather demand can exceed replenishment of storage, especially during the 18:00-23:00 peak.

Its staged plan is conservation messaging, then pressure reduction, then further pressure reduction in selected areas if needed. The named Oldenzaal areas are De Essen, De Graven Es and De Thij; acute care, hygiene and safety are priority considerations.

The operator advises at least nine litres per person for three days and asks institutions with visitors or clients to prepare for lower pressure. It monitors demand/availability and would communicate a boil-water advisory separately if needed.

The page describes a conditional 2026 summer plan, not proof that a pressure step is active at retrieval, a pipe/pressure surface, current water quality, event forecast or deterministic T+72 recovery.

evidenceSources.title: E12 — Public care, education, antenna and electricity-planning context snapshot
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 2026-07-03, CC0; DUO snapshot 2026-08-31, CC BY; RDI snapshot 2026-09-02, licence not stated; NBNL sample retrieved 2026-09-02, exact licence identifier not found
supports: No RIVM acute-care department lies inside GM0173. Medisch Spectrum Twente in Enschede is about 10.406 km and Ziekenhuisgroep Twente in Almelo about 18.237 km straight-line from the municipal reference point; both questionnaire rows report 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric roles.

Seventeen DUO education locations are assigned: thirteen primary, three secondary and one other registered education location. They are registered uses, not occupancy, shelter designation, accessibility, staffing, supplies or generator evidence.

Forty-nine RDI antenna sites represent 98 registered antennas: 24 mobile-communication, eight fixed-link, fourteen amateur, two broadcast and one other-mobile sites. They do not reveal coverage, operator, backhaul, power, backup, load, congestion, availability or restoration.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to ODZ Oldenzaal with Coteq/Enexis context, 94.5 MW existing and 61.2 MW required withdrawal, 11.2 MW/56 queued withdrawal requests, 92 MW existing and 63 MW required injection, 7.3 MW/36 queued injection requests and thirteen projects from 2026. It is large-user planning context, not complete municipal coverage or outage state.

evidenceSources.title: E13 — First-72-hour guidance and explicit observation/forecast NoData
evidenceSources.edition: current municipal preparedness page accessed 2026-09-03; deployment observations retrieved 2026-09-02/03 under their source licences and validities
supports: Oldenzaal tells households to prepare an emergency kit for the first 72 hours, follow NL-Alert and official instructions, and use RTV Oost as the Overijssel emergency broadcaster. Guidance does not prove household compliance or a municipal resource/action schedule.

No KNMI ten-minute weather station, KNMI 365-day seismic-event source point, RWS Waterinfo observation point or rolling forecast point is assigned inside GM0173 in the deployment snapshots. Those networks are sparse or scoped and an empty intersection is NoData, not zero weather, water or seismic risk.

No NDW current situation intersects GM0173 in the 2026-09-03T08:43:00Z current-picture snapshot. That is not proof every A1/N-road, viaduct, local street, rail crossing or German continuation is open through T+72.

No public emergency-support-point selection, opening, staffing, stock, accessible capacity, deployment roster or completed recovery-action ledger was found in the reviewed sources. This remains Unknown rather than absent.

identity.summary: GM0173, Oldenzaal, Overijssel and safety region Twente agree across the consumed official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature id, bundle code and bundle name match; the safety-region assignment is unique.
Identity verification does not establish hazard, asset or service calibration.

geography.summary: The official 2025 generalized polygon and generated reference point are internally coherent.
notes: The reference point [6.90526743455187, 52.30936320378356] lies inside the municipal polygon.

Administrative containment does not encode the stuwwal, local catchments, Stakenbeek/Hulsbeek/pond hydrology, sewers, buffers, groundwater, forest fuels, event footprints, viaduct clearance or international rail/road dependencies.

demography.summary: Municipality and neighbourhood resident totals reconcile within CBS small-area rounding.
notes: Municipality population is 32,021; fourteen neighbourhoods sum to 32,020, a one-person difference (-0.003%).
The 25.3% age-65 share and 5,235 one-person households are relevant to assistance demand but do not determine who needs evacuation or priority restoration.
CBS residents omit event-time visitors, commuters, rail passengers and institution occupants. Published visitor estimates cannot be converted to live occupancy.

regionalDetail.summary: All fourteen neighbourhoods and 36 fields are represented, but dynamic population and material service/exposure fields remain incomplete.
notes: Cars per household covers 11/14; district heat and public charging cover 0/14. Missing values remain null rather than zero.
De Thij has 5,895 residents, De Graven Es 5,260 and De Essen 4,450; the same three are named by Vitens as potentially experiencing a further conditional pressure reduction.
Event attendance, school use, care dependence, drinking-water pressure and recreation occupancy are not resident-equivalent statistics and remain Unknown at incident time.

settlements.summary: Two active BAG woonplaatsen and one BRT woonkern are assigned without reported generalized-boundary leakage.
notes: BAG contains Deurningen and Oldenzaal; BRT independently represents the Oldenzaal built-up woonkern.
Settlement metadata is descriptive and is not forced to reconcile with CBS residents or treated as an emergency population surface.

transport.summary: Dutch A/N-road, rail and timetable identities are useful, but the graph omits internal and German operating continuity and cannot support emergency throughput.
notes: A1 and N342 repeated edges are consecutive series segments, never independent redundancy. Several listed N-road lengths are only short border clips.

The graph stops at Dutch municipality links and does not encode the A1 continuation, Oldenzaal-Bad Bentheim rail, German authorities, modes, directional state, hazardous-goods consist or cross-border mutual aid.

Static station/track geometry and 65 GTFS stop areas do not establish train/bus operation, passengers, vehicles, accessible evacuation capacity or route availability. Empty current NDW is Unknown, not open.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative local risk, water, recreation, care and 72-hour guidance exists, but scenario-time roles, resources, states and actions are not represented.
notes: The official context identifies stuwwal rain/drought/heat, local drainage, nature fire, major events, international rail, conditional drinking-water pressure, external acute care and first-72-hour self-preparation.

The simulator selects no local rainfall surface, sewer/control state, ignition/perimeter, event/visitor occupancy, Vitens pressure stage, rail consist/state, hospital acceptance, support-point inventory or accountable action/resource ledger.
A current Phase 1, conditional June drinking-water plan, annual freight total, register row, design decision or empty snapshot retains its exact time and scope and is not a future operating state.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at all checkpoints, but river, pluvial, heat/drinking-water, wildfire and compound outputs contain release-blocking local contradictions.
notes: The focused gate exercised severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services.

River-flood holds exact depth 0.455443 m, severity 0.141346, 2,249 affected and the same eight service values at T+24, T+48 and T+72; deprived person-hours rise from 89,201.274 to 365,154.299. No major-river/local-brook case supports that direct depth.

Pluvial-flood gives 0.422492 m, 3,984 affected and Drainage 0.490394 at T+24, then zero depth/affected and operational status at T+72 without rainfall, sewer, buffer, Stakenbeek, groundwater or passability milestones.

Heatwave gives 24.085383 degrees C, drought 0.496123 and Water 0.585658 at T+24, then the same heat/drought but operational status, zero affected and Water 0.919839 at T+72. It does not select the Vitens demand trigger or pressure stage.

Canonical wildfire gives drought 0.504110, smoke 0.235767, zero local flame and zero affected at T+24. Compound holds 0.436628 m and 14,262 affected at T+48/T+72; all eight service availabilities are also exactly identical while deprived person-hours rise to 1,023,622.157.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused deterministic gate passed bounds, finite values, conservation, reconciliation and cumulative-burden invariants.
notes: One test file and two tests passed in the initial focused run; every preset/checkpoint result remained deterministic and bounded.
Municipality affected population stayed integral and within 0..32,021; local-region population, affected population, demand and delivery reconciled to municipality totals.
A numerically coherent synthetic index is not automatically a calibrated outage, inundation, casualty, route or recovery estimate.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Unrelated hazards share one synthetic neighbourhood order, contradicting Oldenzaal's distinct water, heat, recreation and fire geography.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire have exactly the same complete fourteen-neighbourhood hazard-severity order.

The common order begins Zuid-Berghuizen, Jufferbeek, Het Inslag-De Kleies, Het Hulsbeek and De Essen, independent of hazard source, local 70 mm/hour runoff patterns, hot areas, Vitens pressure districts or ignition geometry.

A controlled hypothetical wildfire source at the official centre of BU01731000 Het Hulsbeek [6.882415308966754, 52.305744840389785] gives flame 0.547832, smoke 0.441277 and 6,802 affected, but ranks the source neighbourhood fourth of fourteen behind unrelated neighbourhoods. The point is a transparent containment probe, not an asserted incident or fuel polygon.

serviceDependencies.summary: Dependency arithmetic is traceable, but exact water, wastewater, power, telecom, care and supply trajectories exceed public physical and operational evidence.
notes: NWB roads are restricted to Mobility and assumed road Supply, which avoids direct utility-topology fabrication, but non-road service gateways remain synthetic.

RWZI design, 81 weirs, a Vitens staged plan, Coteq/Enexis capacity planning, 49 antenna sites, schools and hospitals supply context only; their connected topology, live compatible capacity, power/backup, state and restoration are unavailable.

The heat scenario's exact water values and compound exact service values are not Vitens pressure forecasts, operator outages or measured delivery. External hospital identity and straight-line distance do not establish acceptance or access.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic ledgers reconcile mathematically, but local hazard, network and action provenance is insufficient for operational interpretation.
notes: Hazard and service contribution ledgers sum to their outputs and dependency-chain arithmetic is inspectable.

There is no selected authority scenario, event-valid weather/pressure/route state, local hydraulic or fire footprint, operator incident identifier, action owner, resource quantity, completion time or observation residual behind the exact values.
Current, forecast, planned, static and synthetic evidence classes must remain visibly separate in exports and the UI.

recovery72h.summary: First-72-hour recovery labels and precise service curves are not caused by accountable Oldenzaal actions, resources or verified completion evidence.
notes: Pluvial becomes operational with zero affected by T+72, wildfire becomes operational after zero direct local fire, and heat becomes operational with zero affected while forcing remains nonzero.
Compound retains the same depth, affected count and all eight service values at T+48/T+72, showing a plateau rather than observed action-linked restoration.

First-72-hour guidance establishes self-preparation, alerts and information channels but no selected support points, personnel, water distribution, traffic control, shelter, care transfer, repair crew, mutual aid or completed milestone.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, settlements and resident population reconcile.
findings.evidence: E01-E02 verify GM0173, its contained centre, 32,021 residents, fourteen neighbourhoods, two BAG woonplaatsen, one BRT woonkern, unique safety-region assignment and nine Dutch logical road links. Neighbourhood population differs by only one person (-0.003%).
findings.action: Retain the official identity/boundary, independent BAG/BRT roles, transparent one-person allocation reconciliation and field-level null semantics; do not alter rounded source observations.

findings.summary: The major-river preset contradicts Oldenzaal's documented stuwwal screen by publishing sustained exact local inundation.
findings.evidence: E03 says direct Dinkel-overflow effects are negligible for Oldenzaal because of the stuwwal. The simulator instead publishes exactly 0.455443 m, 2,249 affected and unchanged service values from T+24 through T+72 without a selected Dinkel, Stakenbeek, Hulsbeek, drainage, defence or inundation case.
findings.action: Suppress direct major-river depth/affected claims for GM0173 unless an authority-reviewed local scenario footprint is selected. Model brook/runoff/pluvial and indirect regional supply effects separately; render unsupported local depth and hotspots Unknown.

findings.summary: Exact pluvial depth and automatic recovery ignore Oldenzaal's elevation, runoff, sewer, buffer and receiving-water mechanisms.
findings.evidence: E03-E05 document a stuwwal, rain-fed beeks/ponds, low areas, viaduct flooding, Blue Arteries, buffers, Stakenbeek works and a coupled RWZI system. The preset produces 0.422492 m and 3,984 affected at T+24, then zero depth/affected at T+72 without local rainfall, groundwater, sewer/control state, storage, receiving water, passability or completion evidence.
findings.action: Bind pluvial output to a versioned local rainfall/runoff surface plus sewer, groundwater, storage, stream and road-threshold evidence. Until then, label amplitude as synthetic and local depth, asset state and recovery as Unknown.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse exactly one full fourteen-neighbourhood severity order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Zuid-Berghuizen, Jufferbeek, Het Inslag-De Kleies, Het Hulsbeek and De Essen first through fifth, followed by the same remaining order. E03-E04, E09 and E11 require hazard-specific rain, heat, recreation and pressure geography.
findings.action: Replace the common seeded ranking with hazard-specific eligibility and intensity surfaces; add permutation/containment tests that fail when unrelated hazards reuse one complete order without shared evidence.

findings.summary: Canonical wildfire omits local flame, and a controlled Het Hulsbeek source fails source-neighbourhood priority.
findings.evidence: E07-E09 establish woodland/recreation, time-critical evacuation and event exposure at Het Hulsbeek. Canonical wildfire gives zero local flame and zero affected at T+24. A hypothetical source at BU01731000's official centre yields flame 0.547832 and 6,802 affected, yet Het Hulsbeek ranks fourth of fourteen, proving source geometry does not dominate the spatial allocation.
findings.action: Require an explicit incident or named exercise with fuel/land-cover eligibility, event-valid wind and moisture, perimeter/spread, transient people, access, extinguishing water and suppression actions. Add a source-containment regression before publishing neighbourhood fire consequences.

findings.summary: Heat-related drinking-water output ignores Vitens' conditional regional demand trigger, staged controls and named Oldenzaal pressure areas.
findings.evidence: E11 identifies a low-reserve connected Noordoost-Twente system, warm-weather/18:00-23:00 demand conditions, staged conservation and pressure reduction, and De Essen, De Graven Es and De Thij as potentially more affected. The heat preset gives exact Water 0.585658 at T+24 and 0.919839 at T+72 without selecting demand observations, an active stage, pressure telemetry, pipe topology or those spatial rules.
findings.action: Implement Vitens context as a separately named, validity-bound conditional scenario: ingest only published stage/area status, preserve Unknown pressure, and never infer an active reduction or recovery from a dated preparedness page. Use the three named neighbourhoods only when the operator stage is selected.

findings.summary: Resident-only affected population omits event, recreation, rail and institutional populations that can dominate Oldenzaal demand.
findings.evidence: E09 reports roughly 20,000 Hulsbeekdag visitors and 100,000-150,000 carnival visitors, compared with 32,021 residents. E10-E12 add international passenger/freight rail, schools and external care dependencies. The model caps and labels affected values as resident-equivalents and does not expose occupancy time, uncertainty or separate evacuation/shelter demand.
findings.action: Keep official residents as baseline, add separate timestamped resident/commuter/visitor/passenger/institution cohorts with source, valid time, uncertainty and reconciliation, and display Unknown when incident-time occupancy is unavailable.

findings.summary: Dutch border-road proxies and static transit points cannot support cross-border rail, hazardous-goods, viaduct, care or evacuation decisions.
findings.evidence: E02 and E10 show the A1/N-road network, Oldenzaal station and active Oldenzaal-Bad Bentheim freight corridor; E06 identifies hazardous substances on rail as a regional scenario; E04 says viaducts can flood; E12 locates acute care outside GM0173. The graph has no German node/authority, rail service/freight state, internal viaduct/road thresholds or time-dependent hospital path.
findings.action: Represent physical corridors once, add explicit road/rail/cross-border modes and authorities, model internal critical crossings and alternate routes, and bind only validity-matched closures/capacities. Keep care, evacuation, supply and repair reachability Unknown without operational evidence.

findings.summary: Exact non-road lifeline trajectories exceed public utility, wastewater, telecom and care topology and state evidence.
findings.evidence: E05 and E11-E13 provide RWZI design, partial water assets, a conditional drinking-water plan, one large-user electricity-planning sample, antenna and facility registers and sparse observations. They do not provide compatible live flow/capacity, connected topology, switching, pressure, backhaul, backup, acceptance, crew or restoration state.
findings.action: Retain provider/asset/register context as non-causal. Gate exact service output on operator topology/state or use clearly labelled synthetic fallback ranges; expose provenance, validity and Unknown fields per service.

findings.summary: First-72-hour status and recovery lack accountable local actions, resources and completion evidence.
findings.evidence: Pluvial, wildfire and heat receive recovery/operational labels without authority milestones, while compound depth, affected population and every service availability are exactly flat at T+48/T+72 as deprived person-hours continue rising. E06-E08, E11 and E13 define governance, staged measures and public guidance but not a selected incident resource/action ledger.
findings.action: Require action owner, trigger, start/completion time, resource quantity, target asset/cohort, evidence class and uncertainty for each restoration delta. Without those fields, label trajectories synthetic and withhold operational/restored claims.

findings.summary: Missing observations, capacities, occupancy and operational states can be mistaken for zero or safe.
findings.evidence: E05 and E12-E13 show null RWZI/weir capacity, no in-boundary RIVM acute care, KNMI station/event or Waterinfo point, no intersecting current NDW situation, and unavailable incident-time visitors, pressure, routes, backup and resources. Each absence has a bounded dataset or access scope and does not prove no asset, no hazard, open routes or service availability.
findings.action: Propagate explicit observed-zero, Unknown, NoData, out-of-coverage, not-applicable and stale states through APIs, maps, statistics, exports and calculations; never coerce them to zero, safe, open, available or recovered.

corrections.summary: Suppress GM0173 direct major-river inundation until a governed local hydraulic footprint is selected.
corrections.validation: For the generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset, GM0173 local flood depth/affected/hotspots must be Unknown or an explicitly reviewed zero screen consistent with E03; local brook/pluvial and indirect supply pathways remain separately unresolved rather than safe.

corrections.summary: Replace Oldenzaal's generic pluvial scalar with source-versioned local rain, terrain, sewer, groundwater, buffer, stream and road-threshold semantics.
corrections.validation: Replay at least one governed local stress case and verify hotspots, depth, drainage and viaduct passability follow the selected surfaces and milestones; if any required state is missing, display Unknown rather than exact depth or automatic clearance.

corrections.summary: Introduce hazard-specific neighbourhood allocation and a controlled Het Hulsbeek wildfire containment gate.
corrections.validation: Fail when unrelated hazard families reuse one complete fourteen-neighbourhood order without common source evidence; in a controlled source-centre exercise, BU01731000 must be first/equal-first or the model must declare its allocation unsupported.

corrections.summary: Add a separate validity-bound Vitens Noordoost-Twente pressure-reduction exercise rather than silently calibrating the generic heat preset.
corrections.validation: Require a selected operator stage, publication/valid time and demand condition; verify no active pressure reduction is inferred from the conditional page alone, and De Essen/De Graven Es/De Thij are used only under the selected further-reduction stage.

corrections.summary: Separate resident, event/recreation, rail-passenger and institutional exposure cohorts.

residualLimitations: The CBS municipality and neighbourhood inputs are 2025 editions with rounded/suppressed small-area values and do not provide incident-time population.
The generalized administrative boundary and centre do not encode elevation, drainage divides, stream geometry, underground assets or operational zones.
The BAG woonplaats Deurningen assignment is official polygon containment but does not mean all of the wider named settlement lies within GM0173.
Cars-per-household values are missing in three neighbourhoods; district heat and public charging values are missing in all fourteen.
The Oldenzaal climate atlas is a modelled vulnerability view toward 2050 and is not a probability, observation or T+72 forecast.
Municipal water-overload guidance and a 70 mm/hour stress case do not provide a live sewer model, remaining storage or verified road thresholds.
The HWH water-asset aggregation is partial; 81 weirs and RWZI Oldenzaal have no usable current capacity, topology, control, power or repair state in the app.
The 2023 RWZI intake/design decision is not a current operating limit, inflow observation, available reserve or restoration forecast.
Vitens' June 2026 page is a conditional seasonal plan and does not prove that any pressure-reduction stage is active at the audit time.
Public drinking-water pipe topology, pressure telemetry, current demand, storage, alternative supply, quality and restoration state are unavailable in the simulator.
The current nature-fire Phase 1 is a timestamped regional operational assessment and cannot be extrapolated through the scenario clock.
No authoritative current ignition, fuel-moisture raster, wind field, fire perimeter, occupancy count, escape-route state, extinguishing-water quantity or suppression forecast was selected.
Published event attendance estimates are historical/planning values and cannot establish incident-time visitor location or evacuation demand.
NWB border links omit local streets, viaducts, crossings, traffic direction, usable emergency throughput and most alternate routes.
The road graph ends at Dutch municipality topology and does not encode German road authorities, live A1 continuation, border controls or mutual-aid capacity.
ProRail geometry, annual freight totals and GTFS schedules do not establish live track, train, passenger, hazardous-goods, bus or station operation.
Straight-line distance to Medisch Spectrum Twente or Ziekenhuisgroep Twente is not ambulance time, passability, acceptance, staffing, beds or capacity.
DUO locations, RDI antennas and the single NBNL capacity sample are register/planning context, not shelter, communications or outage telemetry.
No in-boundary KNMI station/event, RWS Waterinfo point or current NDW situation is a scoped NoData result, not evidence of zero hazard or open infrastructure.
Sensitive physical power, gas, drinking-water, wastewater and telecom topology, backup and restoration resources are not public and must not be invented.
Household 72-hour preparedness advice does not establish compliance, available supplies, selected emergency support points or government response capacity.
No authoritative local action/resource/completion ledger was available to validate the model's precise T+0 to T+72 restoration curves.
